content:
Ashok: quick flag — found an authorization oversight on the sandbox rollout endpoint. canary deploys were being accepted from users in the 'developer' group when feature_flag=beta_sandbox was enabled. not expected. :eyes:
Maria: repro'd locally. steps:
1) login as dev user
2) POST /api/v1/deploys/rollout {
  "env": "sandbox",
  "type": "canary",
  "policy": "percent:10"
}
3) response 202 and rollout started even without ops role

Logs show RBAC check returned 204 (no binding) but request continued. suspect short-circuit in middleware.
Taylor: yikes. is this the new role refactor we merged last week? maybe the role name changed from ops.rollout to ops.deploy and a check missed the alias?
Ashok: exactly my hunch. new migration added ops.deploy but some paths still check for ops.rollout. fallback policy currently allows anyone if both checks are absent.
Kevin: can we add a quick guard to block rollouts from non-whitelisted users until a proper fix? e.g., env var SANDBOX_ROLLOUT_LOCK=true to short-circuit on service start.
Maria: I can patch a middleware guard in staging now. patch will return 403 unless user in rollout_whitelist or has ops.* role. simple and reversible.
Taylor: do that and also add an audit log marker so we can query who triggered the last sandbox rollouts. we need KMS/audit integration to show signer identity for service tokens.
security-bot: Alert: policy-drift-detected in service "deploy-agent". Missing role alias mapping: ops.rollout -> ops.deploy. Last sync: 2026-03-18T14:02:12Z.
Ashok: good. Maria, after your guard, can you also run a DB query to find recent sandbox rollouts by non-ops? sample query I used:```sql
SELECT id, initiator, created_at FROM rollouts WHERE env='sandbox' AND created_at > now() - interval '30 days' AND initiator NOT IN (SELECT user FROM role_bindings WHERE role LIKE 'ops.%');
```
Maria: running that now. preliminary: 4 rollouts in last 7 days by service accounts svc-ci-bot and one by user 'ajenkins' who shouldn't have deploy perms.
Kevin: svc-ci-bot — that sounds like a CI token with broad perms. we recently rotated KMS keys; maybe token got reattached with admin role. need to check KMS binding and key ACLs.
Taylor: action items: 1) Maria deploy guard to staging (in 15m) 2) Ashok to open quick revert PR for last role-refactor if needed 3) Kevin to audit KMS bindings for svc-ci-bot and remove excessive roles 4) Add alert rule for rollout-by-non-ops with high severity
Ashok: I'll open the PR and mark it urgent + add test covering both ops.rollout and ops.deploy aliases. PR link will be posted here.
Maria: guard pushed to staging and rolled. staging rollouts now 403 for dev users. adding audit marker as discussed.
security-bot: Audit entry created: event=rollout_attempt, actor=ajenkins, result=allowed, reason=missing_role_alias, meta={"env":"sandbox","id":"r-7f3b"}
Taylor: can we also surface this in Console -> Security -> Incidents so product ops can triage impact?
Kevin: I'll schedule a brief postmortem if we confirm any customer impact. no signs yet but we should assume internal blast radius.
Ashok: thanks all. follow-ups: KMS ACL prune, role alias map CI job, add unit and integration tests for alias mapping. will update thread with PRs and timeline. :white_check_mark:
